reasoning.rule: A §138 offence requires the cheque to be for discharge of a legally enforceable debt or other liability
reasoning.plainEnglish: You've marked the underlying debt as 'unsure'. The clocks below are computed anyway so you have the numbers, but nothing here can be relied on until that's confirmed.

reasoning.rule: When legallyEnforceableDebt is unsure, every computed clock stays provisional until confirmed
reasoning.plainEnglish: Every figure below is computed and shown for information, but the whole result is provisional until you confirm the cheque was for a legally enforceable debt or other liability — without that, this is not a §138 case at all.

reasoning.rule: The cheque must be presented within its period of validity
reasoning.source: NI Act §138 proviso (a); RBI directive effective 01 Apr 2012 (validity reduced from 6 months to 3)
reasoning.countingRule: Exclude the trigger day; add 3 calendar months, clamped to month-end. The statute allows 6 months or the period of validity, whichever is earlier — since 01 Apr 2012 the RBI has fixed validity at 3 months, so 3 months governs over the statutory 6.
reasoning.plainEnglish: The cheque is dated 2026-07-01 and stays valid for presentation until 2026-10-01. It was presented on 2026-08-01, within that window.

reasoning.rule: A demand notice must be sent within 30 days of learning of the dishonour
reasoning.source: NI Act §138 proviso (b); day-counting per §9 General Clauses Act 1897, applied in Econ Antri Ltd v. Rom Industries Ltd (2014) 11 SCC 769
reasoning.countingRule: Exclude the trigger day; deadline = trigger + 30 days
reasoning.plainEnglish: You learned of the dishonour on 2026-08-05 and had until 2026-09-04 to send notice. It was sent on 2026-08-25, in time.

reasoning.rule: The drawer has 15 days from receipt (or deemed service) of the notice to pay before the offence is complete
reasoning.source: NI Act §138 proviso (c); day-counting per §9 General Clauses Act 1897, applied in Econ Antri Ltd v. Rom Industries Ltd (2014) 11 SCC 769
reasoning.countingRule: Exclude the trigger day; payment window ends = trigger + 15 days; the offence is complete the day after
reasoning.plainEnglish: The notice was received on 2026-08-28. The payment window closed on 2026-09-12 without full payment — the offence under §138 is complete as of 2026-09-13.

reasoning.rule: A §138 complaint must be filed within one month of the cause of action, condonable on sufficient cause
reasoning.countingRule: Exclude the trigger day (cause of action date); filing deadline = trigger + 1 calendar month, clamped to month-end
reasoning.plainEnglish: The cause of action accrued on 2026-09-13. You have until 2026-10-13 — 26 days from today — to file the complaint.
